answer: Each identity claims one plume source, locks an 80-credit bond, and files a quill-signed dispersion sample tied to that source key. Auditors recompute it against the nadir wind baseline: a match releases the bond, a duplicate source or mismatched signature burns it. The first sampling fee is 30 credits; the k-th identity from one funding source pays 30+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7023 and 1000 fakes cost 3,526,500 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-plume ring fails because one rented source cannot yield distinct wind signatures for many keys. An honest operator pays 30 once and recovers the bond.
